chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who has relatives, freed slaves, and orphans who love the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) but do not know the owner of this affair (the Imam). Should they be given from the zakat? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَ هَذَا اَلْأَمْرِ: The owner of this affair (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Are relatives and orphans who love the Imams but do not know them eligible to receive zakat?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that mere affection for the Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali) is insufficient for zakat eligibility if the recipients lack knowledge of the specific Imam (the owner of the funds) in the context of the time. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that 'knowing the Imam' (Ma'rifat al-Imam) is a prerequisite for receiving zakat from the Imam, distinguishing between general love for Ahl al-Bayt and the specific theological recognition required for financial rights. It highlights the distinction between the eight categories in Quran 9:60 and the additional Shia condition of Imamate recognition for funds distributed by the Imam himself.
